text:
Marta: Quick check — we need a final call on the dark-launch routing for residency-constrained tenants. Goal: active/active default, but steer GDPR tenants to EU-local infra without changing client SDKs. Decision needed by EOD.
Aj: Thinking we can surface a lightweight header and a control-plane flag. header: X-Redwood-Residency: eu|us|none. SDKs can add it optionally.
sre-simon: +1 to header. How do we enforce? route-by-header at the edge + owner fallback to local primary. Need an operator-visible metric for misrouted requests.
Chen: Two concerns: 1) header spoofing from untrusted clients — must only be honored if tenant has residency policy in control-plane. 2) what about KV-cache locality? If we route to EU worker but KV is in us-west, latency spikes.
Marta: Good points. Proposal: 1) Edge verifies tenant residency via signed token from control-plane. 2) If residency set -> edge injects X-Res-Verified: true when forwarding.
Aj: Example flow I sketched:
```
client -> edge (checks tenant policy)
edge -> dataplane with headers: X-Redwood-Residency: eu, X-Res-Verified: true
```
Edge takes routing decision based on X-Res-Verified and available capacity.
sre-simon: For caching: we should prefer warm-warm replication for small KV (prefix caches) for residency tenants. Full KV replication is expensive. Maybe prefix-only warmup + regional fallback.
Chen: Agree. Also add a metric: residency_routing_rejects and residency_cache_local_miss. We can use that for canary gating.
Ops: Deploy bot triggered canary for the new header-based route. Are we ready to dark-launch?
deploy-bot: Canary started: region-aware-routing v2 -> 2% traffic (eu/na split). Canary ID: canary-2026-04-residency.
Marta: Ok during canary we only honor X-Redwood-Residency when tenant policy exists; otherwise ignore. Also throttle reroutes to avoid oscillation.
Aj: Config sketch for control-plane policy (read-only snippet):
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "residency": "eu",
  "enforce": true
}
```
We store a signature so edge trusts it.
legal-elaine: Quick legal note — honoring residency by region is fine, but audit logs need to be retained for customers who request evidence. Make sure control-plane stores decision + edge logs for 90 days.
Marta: Noted. We'll add an immutable audit event: residency_decision:{tenant, timestamp, edge, decision}.
Chen: One more operational: fallback policy when EU capacity exhausted. Do we fail closed (reject) or fail open (route to nearest non-EU)? We need tiering per customer.
sre-simon: Offer policy options: strict (reject + 409), degrade (route to dedicated standby EU capacity elsewhere after soft quota), best-effort (route to nearest region). Default to degrade for paid tiers, strict only for legal-mandated tenants.
Marta: Sounds good. Action items: Aj: draft header spec + token signing flow. Chen: caching/replication playbook + metrics. SRE Simon: observability + canary guard rails. Legal Elaine: retention and audit requirements. Ops: monitor canary-2026-04-residency and pause on >0.5% error delta.
Aj: I'll post PR with header spec and edge verification pseudo-code in about 90m.
Chen: I'll simulate cache miss amplification for EU routing and share numbers tomorrow morning.
Marta: Thanks all. If no objections after canary window we flip dark-launch to 20% then 50% over week. Ping me if any blocker. :thumbsup:
